name: 101. Typed resource IDs stay on their upstream endpoint (PR #7307) (resource-id-path-escape)
description:
Pins the fix for the customer report 'Typed resource IDs can escape their intended upstream path' (PR #7307). Before the fix a caller-supplied file/batch/response/container/video id or cached-content name was concatenated into the provider URL; the fasthttp client percent-decodes and then collapses dot segments, so an id like %2e%2e%2fmodels%3f%23 on GET /v1/files/{id}/content reached GET /v1/models with the provider key attached, url.PathEscape-only call sites included, and a Vertex batch name could put a caller-chosen value in the hostname. Providers now validate every id as one opaque path segment (EscapeResourceID) with structured parsers for Gemini collection names, Vertex resource names and Bedrock job ARNs.

Three groups, all free to run (nothing is created): (1) [EXPECT-400] attack ids on every route family must be rejected by Bifrost with 'invalid <field>: ...' and never dispatched, so a 403/404/500 here fails loudly; (2) list -> retrieve chains prove the ids Bifrost itself emits still round-trip when percent-encoded in the path: Gemini files/ and batches/ names, Vertex full resource names in project-number form, Bedrock job ARNs, and the dash/base64 forms on the /openai drop-in; an empty list leaves the variable unset and the chained-var guard skips the consumer; (3) [EXPECT-4XX] well-formed but missing ids must pass the gate and come back as a provider 403/404, which pins the slash-bearing Gemini/Vertex video operation names and the percent-encoded ':provider' video suffix.

item.name: [EXPECT-400] openai native file content: encoded ../models?# (report payload) - #7307

exec: if ([401, 429, 502, 503, 504].indexOf(pm.response.code) !== -1) { return; }
pm.test('path-shaping ID is rejected by Bifrost before provider dispatch', function () {
var t = pm.response.text();
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'ID was not rejected, it may have reached the provider: ' + t.slice(0, 300)).to.equal(400);
pm.expect(t, 'expected the resource ID gate message: ' + t.slice(0, 300)).to.match(/invalid [a-z_]+: /);
